events.description: A single large explosion initiates at ~2.5 s (f1) with a fireball, rapidly expands into a rising smoke/debris column through f8–f10, and begins dissipating by f12.

verification.reason: Frames f1–f12 show a continuous, coherent blast sequence: initial fireball (f1), rapid vertical growth and mushrooming (f2–f8), peak plume (f9–f10), and early dispersion (f11–f12). Candidates 0 (3.5–8.5) and 1 (8.0–15.5) both describe overlapping portions of this same event; the merged interval starts at first visible fireball (f1, 2.5 s) and ends at last clear structured plume before full dispersion (f12, 12.5 s), staying within visible bounds and excluding later residual smoke (f13–f16) and unrelated dust bursts (f19–f23).

rejected.reason: Claims explosion from 11.0 to 25.5 s, but frames f13–f18 show only residual smoke from the first explosion (no new blast), and f19–f23 show a distinct, spatially separate series of synchronized dust puffs along a wall—visually unrelated to the initial vertical plume and lacking blast characteristics (no fireball, no rapid expansion); thus the hypothesis of a single ongoing explosion is contradicted.
